item.title: China’s Top Spy Chief Warns A.I. Is a Threat to Party Rule
item.description: Even as Beijing urges the United States not to hype the dangers of A.I., its own spy chief is framing the technology as a threat to the Communist Party’s security.
item.dc:creator: Lily Kuo
item.category: Beijing Moonshot AI Technology Co Ltd
Ministry of State Security of the People's Republic of China
item.media:description: The Great Hall of the People in Beijing. China’s spy chief called for more party control over A.I. and stricter government oversight of the industry.

item.title: Trump Administration Moves to Integrate A.I. Into Medical Care Despite Concerns
item.description: Federal projects are rolling out A.I. agents that offer therapy and prescribe medicine, raising concerns about safety and the influence of venture capital investors.
item.dc:creator: Christina Jewett
item.category: Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services
item.media:credit: Jeremie Souteyrat for The New York Times
item.media:description: A demonstration of a Limbic A.I. mental health app.

item.title: Trump Rejects Talk of A.I. Regulation and Calls Out Anthropic’s CEO
item.description: The president again rejected calls to try to regulate the industry, even as some of its leaders are speaking more openly about the risks of rapidly developing artificial intelligence.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Swan
item.media:description: President Trump has spent much of his second term aligning himself with promoters of artificial intelligence who have been pushing the U.S. government to clear away obstacles to growth.

item.title: A.I. Queries From Abroad Raise Fears of a Biological Weapons Race
item.description: Today’s chatbots aren’t likely to help lone actors invent a deadly pathogen, experts say. But newer models, trained in biology, may need stronger safeguards.
item.dc:creator: Carl Zimmer
item.media:description: The threat of biological weapons has hung over the world for decades now.

item.title: 10-Year Treasury Yield Touches 5%, Highest Level in Years
item.description: One of the world’s most important interest rates hit a level recorded only once since the global financial crisis, as investors continued to rebuff the Trump administration’s efforts to sway the bond market.
item.dc:creator: Joe Rennison

item.title: Bond Market Rebukes Bessent by Sending Borrowing Costs Ever Higher
item.description: The Treasury secretary had dared “Bloomberg terminal bros” to bet against him and they did.
item.dc:creator: Alan Rappeport
item.media:description: In an interview last week, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent insisted that “Bloomberg terminal bros” are misguided about the state of the Iran war.

item.title: As Supreme Court Weighs Trump Mail Ballot Plan, Another Judge Blocks It
item.description: The ruling by a lower court judge was another blow to President Trump’s effort to make voting by mail harder. The Supreme Court is also considering the Trump plan.
item.dc:creator: Zach Montague
item.media:credit: Alisha Jucevic for The New York Times
item.media:description: The ruling was the second by a federal district judge to find that President Trump’s mail ballot plan is likely illegal.

item.title: The Supreme Court Is Considering Trump’s Mail Voting Plan. Here’s What to Know.
item.description: The administration’s plan to screen mail-in ballots remains blocked as the Supreme Court reviews challenges to new U.S. Postal Service ballot rules.
item.dc:creator: Abbie VanSickle
item.media:description: The Supreme Court is considering challenges to recent a Trump administration plan to restrict mail-in voting through new rules at the U.S. Postal Service.

item.title: Immigrants’ Lawyers Say U.S. Is Redacting Documents Proving Legal Status
item.description: Many noncitizens need immigration records the government has to prove their legal stay and resist deportation. The government is redacting and withholding those documents, lawyers say.
item.dc:creator: Minho Kim
item.media:credit: Alan Nakkash for The New York Times
item.media:description: Federal law mandates that agencies provide immigrants facing deportations needed documents “pertaining to the alien’s admission or presence.”

item.title: ‘Alligator Alcatraz’ Used Small Cages to Confine Migrants, DHS Watchdog Report Says
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security’s internal watchdog provided new details about conditions at the now-shuttered Florida detention center.
item.dc:creator: Madeleine Ngo, Hamed Aleaziz and David Ovalle
item.media:description: President Trump visiting the detention center known as Alligator Alcatraz in Ochopee, Fla., last year.

item.title: Key West Feels the Pain of Trump Decision on Haitians
item.description: The end of legal protections for Haitian immigrants nationally has jolted the labor market in this remote vacation destination in Florida where many live and work.
item.dc:creator: David Ovalle
item.media:credit: Mark Hedden for The New York Times
item.media:description: A Haitian immigrant who works at a supermarket in Key West leaves home less often since losing Temporary Protected Status in July.

item.title: States and Cities Sue Over Trump’s Policy to Restrict Green Cards
item.description: The policy would give immigration officers wide authority to deny green cards to people using public benefits.
item.dc:creator: Madeleine Ngo
item.media:credit: Jamie Kelter Davis for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Trump administration policy would make it harder for immigrants to obtain green cards if they use public assistance, such as the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program.

item.title: How to Watch the 2026 Emmy Awards
item.description: NBC is broadcasting the Monday night ceremony, which will be hosted by Mariska Hargitay.
item.dc:creator: John Koblin
item.media:description: The 78th Emmy Awards will honor shows that aired between June 2025 and May 2026.

item.title: Be the First to Find Out the 100 Best TV Shows of the 21st Century
item.description: Starting Sept. 21, we’ll unveil a list of 100, as voted on by more than 500 television professionals in Hollywood and around the world. Make sure you’re getting updates.
item.dc:creator: The New York Times

item.title: Saudi Arabia Faces ‘Worst-Case Scenario’ After Iran’s Attacks and Trump’s Rebuffs
item.description: The kingdom is in a state of strategic shock after coming under attack from an emboldened Iran and failing to win more U.S. military support, analysts say.
item.dc:creator: Vivian Nereim
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: A satellite photo from Vantor shows the Saudi Arabia East-West pipeline, after it was attacked last week.

item.title: Saudi Leader Meets U.S. Commander as Houthi Attacks Threaten Oil Markets
item.description: Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman asked the United States for more U.S. military help last week after the Iranian-backed Houthi forces in Yemen launched a broad offensive.
item.dc:creator: Eric Schmitt and Aaron Boxerman
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: Saudi Arabia’s crown prince, Mohammed bin Salman, last month. Prince Mohammed held talks on Monday with Adm. Brad Cooper, who leads U.S. Central Command.

item.title: Oil Prices Jump as Attacks Choke Off Saudi Energy Supply
item.description: Traders sold oil futures on concerns that energy supplies from the Persian Gulf would be further diminished by a drone attack on a critical pipeline in Saudi Arabia.
item.dc:creator: Jenny Gross and Gregory Schmidt
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)

item.title: Bob Mackie, Designer Who Bedazzled Carol Burnett and Cher, Dies at 87
item.description: His sequined gowns and outrageous costumes threw clouds of glitter at American fashion for over half a century.
item.dc:creator: Penelope Green
item.media:description: Bob Mackie in 2001.

item.title: Mahmoud Khalil Says Columbia Failed to Protect Pro-Palestinian Students
item.description: In a federal lawsuit, Mr. Khalil and other former student activists say the university was deliberately indifferent to their harassment even before the 2023 Hamas attacks.
item.dc:creator: Sharon Otterman
item.media:credit: Scott Heins for The New York Times
item.media:description: Mahmoud Khalil said his asks to Columbia University administrators to help protect him against the threats he was receiving went unanswered.

item.title: ‘I Have a Lot to Say’: Brain Implant Helps a Disabled Patient Speak
item.description: In the latest advance in brain-computer interfaces, a company said its wireless device enabled speech even when a patient just imagined saying words.
item.dc:creator: Pam Belluck
item.media:description: A woman with a paralyzing disease used a brain implant to converse in real time, even while simply imagining the words, the device company reported.

item.title: Taryn Simon’s Giant Exhibition at the Guggenheim Tells the Story of America
item.description: Taryn Simon’s new show at the Guggenheim Museum is an audacious attempt to document the story of modern America through the life of one F.B.I. agent.
item.dc:creator: Sasha Weiss
item.media:credit: Stephen Shore for The New York Times
item.media:description: Simon during the installation of her Guggenheim show. “You feel it on some cellular level,” she says of the huge effort behind her photographic projects. “All these little steps. This is what makes it of value.”

item.title: In Hegseth’s Pentagon, Top Leaders Battle Turmoil
item.description: Persistent distractions are feeding a climate of mistrust as the U.S. military faces a series of wartime issues, including shortfalls of missile interceptors.
item.dc:creator: Greg Jaffe
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:description: Many current and former military leaders describe Pete Hegseth as a secretary of defense increasingly at war with the institution he runs.

item.title: Risks for Clicks: Why Online Influencers Push Shock Content
item.description: A growing number of social media creators are pushing the boundaries of safety and good taste to feed algorithms and win followers.
item.dc:creator: Mark Walker

item.title: A Teen Autopsy Marks the Arrival of a Deadly Drug in San Francisco
item.description: City officials — and one determined mother — are working to stop the spread of cychlorphine, which is far more potent than fentanyl.
item.dc:creator: Heather Knight
